original_question: Let K be a locally compact subfield of Cv , and suppose that the algebraic closure K̄ of K is dense in Cv . Let f ∈ K(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2. Then f has no wandering domains.
target_in_paper: Conjecture 17.6 in Section 17 ("p-adic and Nonarchimedean Dynamics"), as motivated by Theorems 17.4 and 17.5.
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the official statement of Conjecture 17.6 almost verbatim: it has the correct hypotheses on K (locally compact subfield of C_v with dense algebraic closure), the correct class of maps f in K(z), the correct degree restriction deg(f) >= 2, and the correct conclusion that there should be no wandering domains.
missing_details: The ambient field C_v should be introduced as an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value |.|_v.
The paper is working on the Berkovich projective line P^1_Berk over C_v, not merely on the classical projective line P^1(C_v).
"Wandering domain" should be defined explicitly as a connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f that is not preperiodic under iteration.
The statement is an open conjecture/question in the paper, not a proved theorem.
For full stand-alone clarity, one should say that the rational function f in K(z) induces a self-map of P^1_Berk, whose Fatou components are under discussion.
If one writes "the algebraic closure Kbar of K is dense in C_v," it is best to clarify that Kbar is the algebraic closure of K inside C_v.
refined_question: Let C_v be an algebraically closed field complete with respect to a nonarchimedean absolute value |.|_v, let K be a locally compact subfield of C_v whose algebraic closure in C_v is dense in C_v, and let f in K(z) be a rational function of degree at least 2, viewed as an induced self-map of the Berkovich projective line P^1_Berk. Must every connected component of the Berkovich Fatou set F_f be preperiodic under iteration; equivalently, does f have no wandering domains?
justification: The draft is targeting Conjecture 17.6 exactly, not a broader neighboring problem. The wording of the draft coincides with the conjecture itself, whereas Theorem 17.4 adds extra hypotheses about wild recurrent critical points and so is not the exact target. The nearby context in Section 17 supplies the missing stand-alone ingredients: the nonarchimedean setup for C_v and P^1_Berk, the definition of the Berkovich Fatou set, and the definition of a wandering domain. The paper also explains that Theorem 17.5 gives explicit wandering-domain examples once the locally compact coefficient-field hypothesis is dropped, and that the contrast between Theorems 17.4 and 17.5 is what leads to Conjecture 17.6. The refined question therefore keeps your draft narrow, faithful, and self-contained without drifting to the later stronger-but-different Conjecture 17.8.
